lines.en: label wakanaspring5:
I can’t show you what I look like. I can’t mimic how she speaks.
But I’ll hold your hand and weep with you when tragedy repeats.
Because time is sure to take me next — and when it does, don’t fret.
Just leave my ashes on display somewhere you won’t forget.

scene wakanathefriend1
I AM VERY SAD
But I’m sure you probably get that already since I’ve always been sad and have gone through various phases in which that sadness is heavier than normal. Like when I raped Molly or killed Maya.
scene wakanathefriend2
THIS IS ANOTHER ONE OF THOSE TIMES
Just this time probably won’t last as long because I’ve got battle-hardened skin now and could stop a truck with my cock-flesh if it approached me at top speed during sex.
TODAY, I TAKE THE TRASH OUT

It’s why I got out of bed. They call it “responsibility” in other parts of the world (the ones I will never see) ///Weebnote/Godnote: “World” in this context is in relation to the world not the World.
scene wakanathefriend3
it looked something like this (get it haha wrong image still relevant so DEEP)
The takeout menus are still on the table from when Niki left for the beach and one of Ami’s socks is in the dryer. I can’t bring myself to move either.
THERE IS NOTHING ON TV
scene lr_day
Okay, I’m good now.
Just needed to get that out of the way really quickly before I make a phone call to redeem a friendship coupon.
The bright side of everyone leaving me is that I can pretty much bring anyone I want over here now without risking getting in trouble. Maybe.
Technically, Niki could come back at any moment and pretend she still loves me as more than just a stray dog she made the mistake of taking in.
Just she hasn’t yet. She’s been gone for a while. And I’d be really worried about her fucking some other guy if she knew any and all of them weren’t up in space dying from asphyxiation or whatever.
Anyway, phone time.
I tap on Wakana’s name in my phone and-
: Hello?
Oh thank god.
: Hey. So remember that time you were really miserable and needed me to come over so you could cry into my shoulder and make me buy you dinner?
: I’m sorry, but I think you have the wrong number. Please don’t call here again. Goodbye.
: Wakana, I could really use your company.

: I’ve been standing in the middle of my living room staring at the floor for I think thirty minutes now. And I imagine that is what I will do for the rest of the day if you don’t come snap me out of it.
: Oh good. We can be miserable together then. I’ll shower and head over in twenty minutes.
: Great. But I get to be the more miserable one today since you had your turn already.
: Okay. But that doesn’t mean I won’t be silently competing with you in my own head.
: I also expect a hug.
: Jesus, Arakawa. Are you fucking dying?
: No. I just miss you and you smell nice and no one touches me in this house anymore.
: Perhaps I’ll bring a ball-gag as well if it’ll get you to stop this infantile whimpering.
: Can I make you wear it instead?
: Will that make you feel better?
: Probably, yeah.
: Then no. See you in half an hour.
scene black
Wakana hangs up the phone and I know that these thirty minutes will pass by in no time at all since I’ve already been standing here for that long.
scene wakanathefriend4
See? She’s already here and I didn’t even have to let her inside. Not locking the door worked out in my favor for once.
: Wow, Arakawa. You look terrible.
: Do I really? I took a bath this morning and thought I looked mostly normal.
: You do. That’s exactly the problem.
: Oh. So you’re just being mean again. Got it.
scene wakanathefriend5
: I didn’t want to shock you by caring so much as soon as I walked in. But, now that I’m here, you can cry if you want and I’ll only make fun of you a little bit.
: I don’t need to cry. Or want to. In fact, I’m not sure I even remember how. I just knew that being alone wasn’t going to be good for me and-
: And you didn’t have the energy to go visit any of your many fan-clubs popping up throughout the city?
: I can’t tell if that’s in reference to the students or if Nodoka’s book is suddenly getting even more popular.
scene wakanathefriend4
: I’ve been meaning to read that. Nagasawa is quite talented despite being utterly unbearable in practically every other way.
: Don’t. Just hug me instead. I am ready.
scene wakanathefriend5
: Why stop at a hug when you can have something even better than that, Arakawa?
scene wakanathefriend6
: What?
: After all you’ve done for me in my times of need, I think it’s only fair that I go the extra mile for you today. Don’t you agree?
: Uhhhhhhh...yes?
: But...
scene wakanathefriend7
: But what?
: Saying that while you’re tying your hair back makes it kind of look like you’re about to steer this “friendship” in a whole new direction that I was not expecting to happen so suddenly.
: I am. But as you know, I have very little experience doing this, so I can’t imagine I’ll do very well.
: I suppose all that matters is that you enjoy it, though. So I’ll try my best even if I hate every second of it.
: What...What about Osako? Is she, like...okay with this?
: She doesn’t know I’m here. And I’d prefer you keep it a secret as well since things are already somewhat confusing between us.
scene wakanathefriend8
: Why the fuck are you acting so weird? Just let it happen.
scene wakanathefriend9
: I mean...if you say so.
: Arakawa? What are-
scene wakanathefriend10
: Oh, for fucking- no! Put it away. I’m going to cook for you, you devious piece of shit. Not do that.
scene wakanathefriend11
: Hah...
: I knew it was too good to be true.
: You’re a filthy, pathetic degenerate. But at least your misery isn’t great enough to kill your libido. I’d say that’s a step forward.
scene wakanathefriend12
: In my defense, you almost word-for-word recreated one of the best dreams I’ve ever had there. I can’t be blamed for giving into the fantasy when I’ve wanted it for so long.
scene wakanathefriend13
: Is that really something you should be telling me while I’m holding multiple knives?
: No. But you weren’t holding them one CG ago, so I don’t think I can be blamed for that either.
: Also, when did you learn how to cook? Because I’m pretty sure you burned soup the last time I watched you try.
: Only because your instructions were horrendous. And also because I can’t cook.
: I feel like one of those things implies that you probably shouldn’t cook today either then. Especially since you didn’t even bring any ingredients.
: I just planned on using whatever you had available. And if I couldn’t find anything, I figured I’d just shave off a piece of you instead and throw that over an open flame.
: I may be disgustingly self-absorbed, but I don’t think it goes as far as wanting to eat myself.
: Then fetch me three ingredients of your choosing. No more than that. Less is okay, though. I need to start small if I am ever going to improve.
: Wakana, I appreciate the sentiment. But, as miserable as I am, I don’t think I want to die today. And for that reason, I am unable to try your cooking.
scene wakanathefriend14
: It wasn’t so much the food that I was expecting you to enjoy, but the act of watching me fail at something since it is so exceedingly rare as I am already better than you at everything.
: Now that you mention it, that does sound exciting. I’m not really sure it’s going to cheer me up, though.
: Well, what do you suggest then? And don’t take that as an opportunity to unzip yourself again as I will not be found liable if I accidentally cut it off.
scene wakanathefriend15
: A movie and junk food — what an ordinary suggestion from someone I nearly had to castrate just a short while ago.
: This is what I’d normally do with Ami and Niki when they didn’t hate my guts. I’m just trying to breathe some sort of normalcy back into this place.
scene wakanathefriend16
: Since when does Arakawa Jr. hate you? The two of you have always been sickeningly close from what I’ve seen.
: I like how you don’t question Niki suddenly hating me. Just Ami.
: Well, yeah. That one makes a little more sense to me with how frequently you’re screwing our co-worker in public bathrooms.
: If it’s okay, I’d rather not get into the specifics of it. All you really need to know is that Ami left and Niki broke up with me.
: I see...

: Now, is this a situation where you’d like me to be on your side and trash-talk the two of them? Or would you rather, in true Arakawa fashion, have me belittle you instead and tell you it’s all your fault?
: Is there a third option of just silently watching a movie together and maybe falling asleep on the couch?
: There could be if I didn’t actually care. But knowing you went out of your way to ask me here makes me think just sitting in silence together isn’t going to be very helpful in the long run.
scene wakanathefriend17
: I won’t think you’re “weak” if that’s what you’re concerned about. Which I imagine it is since I was concerned about the same thing.
: I already know I’m weak...I can talk about that no problem. It’s everything else that trips me up.
: It’s hard telling someone a story when there are a million details you need to omit and the ones left over make everything sound way too simple.
: You’re a writer. I’m sure you can figure it out.
: See...that’s the thing, though. I can’t.

: And that’s just one more reason I chose poetry as my field of expertise since you don’t always need to tell a full story with that. You can normally just throw out a bunch of dots and have people connect them for you.
: You do know I’m quite adept at connecting those dots, don’t you? And still very interested in reading something of yours.
: Just explain things to me in the simplest way for you and I can assure you I will only judge you a little bit.
: You’re always trying to get me to write, Wakana...no matter what the situation is.
: Indeed. I am. And I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t annoyed by the fact you’ve never budged on that and have elected instead to just do nothing whenever you’re feeling down instead.
: You’ve got a perfectly good outlet waiting for you that you won’t even attempt to use. It’s like you’re some sort of mental masochist or something.
: Writers need to write. That’s how we’ve learned to feel. You not doing that even when I’m pushing you to is like making me watch you set yourself on fire.
: And I really hate that, Arakawa. I don’t want you to suffer more than you already have.
: Writing is suffering though, Wakana. How am I supposed to do that when all it does is remind me of what I’ve lost?
scene wakanathefriend18
: Are you gonna say something? Or is that the end of this conversation?
: Frankly, Arakawa — I’m not sure what I’m allowed to say at this point when you’ve already threatened our friendship over this subject before.
: Like I said, I’m good at connecting the dots. But when I’m told to stop doing that and you try to push me to, I can’t help but feel a little trapped.
: Then, if I lift the embargo on talking about what I’m sure you’ve already figured out...will that get you to stop trying to make me write?
scene wakanathefriend19
: But it’ll make me happy knowing you trust me enough to talk to me about it.
: It’s never been about trust. It’s about not wanting to feel like there’s a bomb inside of me just waiting to go off.
: And it’s really the way you felt about her that’s causing that? Not...what happened?
: You wouldn’t understand.
: Arakawa, barring your niece or daughter or whatever you want to call her, I’ve read the Girl Who Cannot Breathe more than probably anyone you know. Do you know why?
: Because you’re nosy and obsessed with weird poets?
: Because it’s the only way I can learn more about you when you won’t tell me anything.
scene wakanathefriend20
: And I guess maybe I’m a little nosy too...but only because I care.
: And I imagine you’d do the same thing if you found out I had a secret romance with an older man as a child.
: You concede that it was romance, then?
scene wakanathefriend21
: From a moral standpoint, no...
: But I’m willing to acknowledge that no third party can ever truly understand the feelings two other people have for each other.
: And between what I’ve read from her work and how greatly her existence impacted you...it’d be foolish to not acknowledge the existence of some form of love there.
: It makes me a little sick to my stomach, though...the Boy, or...you, since I guess we’re finally addressing this is...
: Well...he always appears so...helpless...and innocent in her poetry. Like he didn’t fully understand what was going on. Which, given how old you must have been...
: It was true at first.
scene wakanathefriend22
: I idolized her...Thought she must have been some sort of angel. So when she wanted to spend more time with me, I happily obliged.
: I’d have accepted anyone back then...and I’m just lucky it was someone who really seemed to care about me.
: So when it got sexual, I never really...tried to stop her. Not seriously, at least. Especially knowing that doing so would likely form a rift in the only good relationship I ever had.
: I just didn’t want to lose her. And the more time we spent together, the more I realized just how important she was to me. Or...is.
: I can still see her sometimes. Smell her. And...you know, it’ll sound weird, but I can almost feel her hanging over my shoulder every time I pick up a pen. Correcting me...making suggestions.
: I just...I want to avoid that because it hurts too much. And I thought that might change when I stopped holding back the memories, but...no luck.
: So now here I am, miserable again with no way to express it, and the ones I’ve held closest suddenly giving up on me.
: I haven’t given up on you, Arakawa.
: I could make you if I wanted to...and it’d be really easy.
: Try me.
: No...That’s how easy I know it would be.
: What would make you feel better then? Right now. Apart from a blowjob.
: I don’t know...handjob, maybe?
scene wakanathefriend23
: Arakawa, be serious. I came here to try and help you and I feel like all I’ve done is make things worse.
: You haven’t made anything worse. I’ve been trying to be more open about stuff and...I know how badly you wanted to talk about this, so I kind of expected it to happen soon enough.
: But right now, I...
: ...You, what?
: Don’t make fun of me, okay?
: I’ll do my best.
: I just want Ami to come home.
scene wakanathefriend24
: I’ve really fucked her up, Wakana.
: I’m sure I don’t need to tell you how hard it would be growing up with me as a father.
: Probably not as bad as you think if you feel that strongly about her. That was the most human thing I’ve ever heard you say.
: You’ve seen her in school, right? Does she seem normal?
: I’ve seen her in the halls, but I haven’t talked to her.
: I could, though...I should be able to free up some time in my schedule.
: And, in the event that I do, is there anything you’d like me say? Any sort of message you’d like to convey?
: Just tell her I’m sorry.
: Are you sorry? For whatever it is that happened and forced the two of you apart?
: Not really. But I’m not above lying if it makes my life a little easier.
scene wakanathefriend25
: Oh? Do you ever lie to me?
: Probably. I can’t really think of any examples off the top of my head though.
: Guess I’ll have to look out then.
: How about you, Wakana? Do you ever lie to me?
scene wakanathefriend26
: Mhm. All the time.
scene wakanathefriend27
: Like you said...makes life easier.
: Guess I’ll have to look out too, then.
: Don’t look too hard. You might not like what you see.
: I don’t know...I feel like I could look at you all day and like every second of it.
: Suspicious thing to say right after telling me you habitually lie to me all the time.
: Did I say “habitually?” Because I’d like you to think my lies are much more rare than that.
: And I’d like you to stop staring at me...
: It’s making me sick.
scene black
: Fine. Guess I’ll finally put a movie on now that my sob story is over.
: And with a lot less crying than mine. Color me impressed, Arakawa. I brought a handkerchief for you and everything. I was really hoping for tears.
: Maybe next time. Any Netflix suggestions?
: Mmm...don’t hate me. Dead Poets Society.
: Get out of my house.
